newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Bosnia presidency agrees meet in Sarajevo.
newsitem.headline: Bosnia presidency agrees meet in Sarajevo.

text.p: Serb, Croat and Moslem members of Bosnia's newly-elected collective presidency were due to meet on Monday in Sarajevo after days of haggling over the venue for their first session, Bosnian government and Serb officials said.
The three men agreed to hold their inaugural meeting in the Konak building in Sarajevo's old town, Moslem and Serb officials told Reuters.
The presidency, charged with governing a union of Serb and Moslem-Croat territories, was chosen in Bosnia's first post-war general elections on September 14.
Alija Izetbegovic, a Moslem, won most votes in the presidential race and will serve as the body's chairman for a two-year term.
Izetbegovic narrowly defeated Serb Momcilo Krajisnik for the chairman's post. Kresimir Zubak was elected as the Croat representative.
Krajisnik had said earlier he did not feel safe meeting in the city centre and wanted the presidency to convene on the boundary line between the Serb republic and the Moslem-Croat federation.
International mediators and Izetbegovic dismissed Krajisnik's proposal as a violation of the spirit of the Dayton peace agreement which ended the 3 1/2-year Bosnian war.
Krajisnik, a hardline nationalist who led a separatist Serb rebellion against Bosnia's bid for independence from old Yugoslavia, has not set foot in Sarajevo since the war erupted in April 1992.
